units.title: Art: Line and Shape
units.big_idea: Artists use many kinds of lines and shapes to show movement, feeling, and ideas.

units.title: Music: Steady Beat and Rhythm
units.big_idea: Music has a steady beat, and rhythms are patterns of long and short sounds we can read and write.

units.title: Art: Color and Mood
units.big_idea: Colors can be mixed, and artists choose colors to create a mood.

units.title: Music: Melody and Pitch
units.big_idea: Melodies move up, down, and stay the same, and we can sing, play, and write them.

units.title: Art: Texture, Form, and Sculpture
units.big_idea: Artists create texture and three-dimensional forms, and everyday objects can be repurposed into art.

units.title: Music: Instruments, Timbre, Dynamics, and Tempo
units.big_idea: Each instrument has its own sound, and composers use loud/soft and fast/slow to tell stories.

units.title: Art Around the World
units.big_idea: People in different times and places make art for celebrations, everyday use, and storytelling.

units.title: Dance and Drama
units.big_idea: Bodies and voices can tell stories through movement and pretend play.

units.title: Create and Compose: My Community
units.big_idea: Artists and musicians create works about their own lives and communities and prepare them to share.

units.title: Showcase
units.big_idea: Sharing art and music with an audience celebrates our growth.

objectives: Identify and draw straight, curved, zigzag, wavy, spiral, and dotted lines
Use lines to show movement and feeling
Set up and clean up art tools safely

days.title: Line hunt
days.work: Walk inside and outside to find 10 kinds of lines (fence, branches, stairs, waves on a rug) and sketch each in a new sketchbook.

days.title: Line sampler
days.work: Fold paper into 12 boxes and fill each with a different line type using markers; label each line.

days.title: Lines show feelings
days.work: Listen to calm and energetic music and draw lines that match each; discuss which lines feel calm or excited. Practice art-tool cleanup routine.

days.title: Yarn lines
days.work: Drop pieces of yarn on paper, trace the shapes they make, and turn them into an imaginative drawing.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Share the line sampler and say which line is your favorite using art words (zigzag, curved, thick, thin).

weeks.assessment: Line sampler with labeled line types and oral reflection.

objectives: Look at and describe Kandinsky's art
materials: image of Kandinsky's 'Squares with Concentric Circles'

days.title: Shape sort
days.work: Sort cut-paper shapes into geometric (circles, squares, triangles) and organic (leaf, puddle, cloud) and find both kinds in your home.

days.title: Look at Kandinsky
days.work: Look at Kandinsky's 'Squares with Concentric Circles' and describe the shapes, colors, and patterns you see.

days.title: Concentric circles
days.work: Draw a 3x4 grid and fill each square with concentric circles in oil pastel, using different colors in each ring.

days.title: Finish and add
days.work: Finish the Kandinsky-style grid and add a border of geometric shapes.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Tell which square you like best and why, using the words geometric, pattern, and contrast.

weeks.assessment: Kandinsky-inspired circles artwork and reflection.

days.title: Look at Matisse
days.work: Look at Matisse's 'The Snail' and learn that he 'drew with scissors' when he was ill; describe the shapes and colors.

days.title: Free cutting
days.work: Practice safe scissor use and cut 10 organic shapes freehand without drawing first, inspired by leaves and seaweed.

days.title: Compose
days.work: Arrange the shapes on a background in three different ways before gluing; take a photo of each arrangement and choose the best.

days.title: Positive and negative
days.work: Use the leftover paper (negative space) to make a second collage and compare the two.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Present both collages and explain why you chose your arrangement.

weeks.assessment: Matisse-style collage and explanation of choices.

weeks.topic: Line and shape project: Mondrian and my neighborhood
objectives: Use lines and shapes to plan an artwork
Compare artists' use of line and shape

days.title: Look at Mondrian
days.work: Compare Mondrian's 'Broadway Boogie Woogie' with Kandinsky's circles; list how each artist used lines and shapes.

days.title: Neighborhood map art
days.work: Sketch the streets near your home as vertical and horizontal lines on paper.

days.title: Mondrian city
days.work: Turn the sketch into a Mondrian-style artwork with black lines and red, yellow, and blue rectangles.

days.title: Mini gallery
days.work: Hang the unit's artworks in a hallway 'gallery' and label each with title and materials.

days.title: Unit 1 check
days.work: Give a gallery tour naming 5 kinds of lines and both kinds of shapes in your work.

weeks.assessment: Mondrian-style artwork and gallery tour using art vocabulary.

objectives: Keep a steady beat with body and instruments

days.title: Heartbeat
days.work: Feel your heartbeat and compare it to a steady beat; pat the beat to Sousa's 'The Stars and Stripes Forever.'

days.title: Beat chart
days.work: Point to 8 hearts on a beat chart while chanting 'Engine, Engine Number Nine' and other rhymes.

days.title: Beat vs. rhythm
days.work: Pat the beat while clapping the words of 'Twinkle, Twinkle' and explain the difference between beat and rhythm.

days.title: Marches and waltzes
days.work: March to music in 2 and sway to a waltz in 3 (Strauss's 'Blue Danube'); count 1-2 and 1-2-3.

days.title: Check
days.work: Keep a steady beat on spoons with 3 songs while a parent checks; explain beat in one sentence.

weeks.assessment: Steady-beat performance check.

weeks.topic: Reading rhythm: ta, ti-ti, and rest
objectives: Read quarter notes, eighth-note pairs, and quarter rests

days.title: Ta and ti-ti
days.work: Learn the quarter note (ta) and eighth-note pair (ti-ti) and clap 8 four-beat flash cards.

days.title: Rest
days.work: Learn the quarter rest (silent beat) and read patterns with rests; play 'rhythm echo' with a parent.

days.title: Word rhythms
days.work: Match food words to rhythms (pie = ta, apple = ti-ti, watermelon = ti-ti ti-ti) and write 4 food-word rhythms.

days.title: Play rhythms
days.work: Play written rhythms on rhythm sticks, pots, or a drum while keeping a steady beat.

days.title: Check
days.work: Read and clap 6 new four-beat rhythms accurately and write 2 rhythms that a parent claps.

weeks.assessment: Rhythm reading and writing check.

materials: recordings of 'We Will Rock You' style beats

days.title: Body percussion
days.work: Learn four body-percussion sounds (stomp, pat, clap, snap) and echo 10 four-beat patterns led by a parent or video.

days.title: Ostinato
days.work: Perform a repeated rhythm ostinato while a parent sings 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat.'

days.title: Bucket drumming
days.work: Use a bucket or pot to play two layered rhythms with a family member.

days.title: Improvise
days.work: Improvise 4-beat answers to rhythm 'questions' clapped by a parent.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a layered body-percussion piece (stomp-pat-clap-snap ostinato under a chanted rhyme) for the family and keep a steady beat throughout.

weeks.assessment: Body-percussion performance.

objectives: Compose a rhythm piece in 4 beats

days.title: Measures
days.work: Learn bar lines and measures in 4/4 and draw 4 measures with rhythms.

days.title: Compose
days.work: Compose a 4-measure rhythm piece using ta, ti-ti, and rest and write it on cards.

days.title: Digital rhythm
days.work: Recreate your piece in Chrome Music Lab Rhythm and listen to it.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice your piece on a homemade shaker or pot drum, circling and slowly repeating the trickiest measure until it is steady.

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Perform your composition and explain why you chose your rhythms.

weeks.assessment: Rhythm composition performance and notation.

materials: tempera or watercolor paints (red, yellow, blue)

days.title: Primary colors
days.work: Learn red, yellow, blue as primary colors and paint three blobs; practice brush washing routine.

days.title: Mixing
days.work: Mix orange, green, and purple on a paper plate palette and record each recipe.

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Paint a 6-part color wheel on a paper plate.

days.title: Color hunt
days.work: Find objects at home in each color of the wheel and photograph or draw them.

days.title: Check
days.work: Name primary and secondary colors and explain how to mix each.

weeks.assessment: Painted color wheel and oral check.

weeks.topic: Warm and cool colors and mood
objectives: Paint with a warm or cool palette
materials: image of Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night'

days.title: Warm and cool sort
days.work: Cut 12 pictures from magazines and sort them into warm-color and cool-color piles; describe how each pile makes you feel.

days.title: The Starry Night
days.work: Look closely at Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' for 3 minutes, then describe its mood, colors, and swirling lines using 'I see… I think… I wonder…'.

days.title: Cool night painting
days.work: Paint a night sky over your own house using only cool colors and swirling brushstrokes like Van Gogh.

days.title: Warm sunset
days.work: Paint a sunset over the same house using only warm colors.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Hang both paintings side by side and tell how changing the palette changed the mood, using the words warm, cool, and mood.

weeks.assessment: Warm and cool paintings with oral mood comparison.

objectives: Make tints and shades of a color

days.title: Value strip
days.work: Make a 7-step value strip from one color by adding white (tints) on one side and black (shades) on the other.

days.title: Monet's Water Lilies
days.work: Look at Monet's 'Water Lilies' and notice the short brushstrokes and many tints of blue and green; describe the time of day you think it shows.

days.title: Paint outside
days.work: Sit outside like Monet and paint a garden, tree, or sky using short dabbed brushstrokes.

days.title: Add light and shadow
days.work: Finish the landscape by adding tints where the sun hits and shades where shadows fall.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Point to 3 tints and 3 shades in your painting and explain how you mixed them.

weeks.assessment: Value strip and observational landscape.

weeks.topic: Color project: a painting with a mood
objectives: Plan an artwork to show a chosen mood
Reflect on artistic choices with others

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a mood (calm, joyful, spooky, excited) and sketch a scene in the sketchbook, noting which colors will show that mood.

days.title: Paint the background
days.work: Paint the background with your chosen palette, using tints and shades for depth.

days.title: Paint the details
days.work: Add the main subject and details with line and shape from Unit 1.

days.title: Guess the mood
days.work: Show the painting to family without telling the mood and have them guess; record their guesses and the clues they used.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Sort 8 artwork images by mood and explain one choice; tell what you would change in your own painting next time.

weeks.assessment: Mood painting, family guesses, and image-sorting check.

objectives: Show melodic direction with body and drawings
Sing in tune with a model
materials: xylophone, piano app, or water glasses

days.title: High or low
days.work: Listen to pairs of notes on a piano app or xylophone and show high (hands up) or low (hands on knees); hear high and low animal sounds.

days.title: Water glass scale
days.work: Fill 5 glasses with different water levels, tap them, and order them from lowest to highest pitch.

days.title: Melody maps
days.work: Draw lines showing the melody of 'Twinkle, Twinkle' going up, down, and staying the same, then follow the map while singing.

days.title: Scarf melody
days.work: Move a scarf up and down to match the melody of 'Frère Jacques' and sing it in tune with a recording.

days.title: Check
days.work: Identify high/low in 8 note pairs and draw the contour of a short melody played by a parent.

weeks.assessment: Pitch identification and melody-contour drawing.

objectives: Sing and sign sol, mi, and la
Read sol-mi-la patterns on a staff

days.title: Sol-mi
days.work: Sing 'Rain, Rain, Go Away' and 'Star Light, Star Bright' with sol-mi hand signs.

days.title: Add la
days.work: Add la with 'Ring Around the Rosie' and echo-sing 8 sol-mi-la patterns with hand signs.

days.title: Penny staff
days.work: Place pennies on a 3-line staff to show sol-mi-la patterns and sing them.

days.title: Improvise
days.work: Improvise a 4-beat sol-mi-la answer to a sung question ('What did you eat today?').

days.title: Check
days.work: Sing 4 patterns from penny-staff notation and echo 4 patterns with hand signs.

weeks.assessment: Solfège singing and reading check.

objectives: Sing folk songs from different cultures
Explain why people sing these songs
materials: recordings of 'De Colores,' 'Funga Alafia,' 'Sakura Sakura,' 'Bluebird, Bluebird'

days.title: De Colores
days.work: Learn the first verse of the Mexican folk song 'De Colores' and discuss what it celebrates.

days.title: Funga Alafia
days.work: Learn the West African welcome song 'Funga Alafia' with movements and sing it as a greeting.

days.title: Sakura
days.work: Listen to 'Sakura Sakura' from Japan, describe its mood, and draw cherry blossoms while listening.

days.title: Singing game
days.work: Play the American singing game 'Bluebird, Bluebird' with family, keeping the beat while moving.

days.title: Rehearse and check
days.work: Choose a favorite folk song, practice the hard parts, and sing it for family, telling where it comes from and why you like it.

weeks.assessment: Folk song performance with spoken introduction.

objectives: Create a short melody using sol, mi, la, and do
Document the melody with notation or recording

days.title: Song Maker
days.work: Explore Chrome Music Lab Song Maker and make 3 short melodies that go up, go down, and repeat.

days.title: Compose
days.work: Compose an 8-beat melody using sol, mi, la, and do on Song Maker or a xylophone; write it on staff paper or with iconic notes.

days.title: Add words
days.work: Add words about a pet or favorite place to your melody.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Play it for a family member, ask for one 'star' and one 'wish,' and revise one part.

days.title: Unit 4 check
days.work: Perform the final melody and explain why you chose its up and down shape.

weeks.assessment: Composed melody (notation or recording) and performance.

days.title: Texture walk
days.work: Touch and describe 10 textures around home and yard (bark, carpet, brick, sponge) and record words for each.

days.title: Rubbings
days.work: Make crayon rubbings of 12 textured surfaces and label each.

days.title: Texture collage
days.work: Cut up rubbings and arrange them into an animal collage (bark for fur, mesh for scales).

days.title: Implied texture
days.work: Draw 4 objects (a pinecone, a sweater, a rock, a feather) using lines and dots to show texture.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Explain the difference between real and implied texture using your collage and drawings.

weeks.assessment: Texture collage and implied-texture drawings.

days.title: 2-D vs. 3-D
days.work: Compare shapes (flat) and forms (sphere, cube, cylinder) using household objects; draw a circle and roll a clay sphere.

days.title: Pinch pot
days.work: Make a pinch pot by pressing a thumb into a clay ball and pinching walls evenly; follow cleanup steps.

days.title: Add texture
days.work: Use forks and toothpicks to press textures into the pot and add a small clay animal handle.

days.title: Dry and paint
days.work: Let the pot dry, then paint it with a pattern using colors from Unit 3.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Show the pot and describe its form and texture and one thing that was hard to make.

weeks.assessment: Finished pinch pot and reflection.

objectives: Build a sculpture from found objects
materials: image of a Louise Nevelson wall sculpture

days.title: Look at Nevelson
days.work: Look at a Louise Nevelson wall sculpture and describe how she turned scraps of wood into art painted all one color.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Brainstorm with family 5 ways to turn recyclables into a sculpture, sketching ideas.

days.title: Build
days.work: Glue boxes, tubes, and caps into a shallow box to create a relief sculpture.

days.title: Paint
days.work: Paint the whole sculpture one color (black, white, or gold) like Nevelson and notice how shadows show the forms.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Discuss with family how painting it one color changed the look and what objects you repurposed.

weeks.assessment: Repurposed relief sculpture and discussion.

objectives: Plan and create an original sculpture

days.title: Plan
days.work: Sketch an animal or creature sculpture from 2 views and list the materials needed.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the main form from clay or recyclables.

days.title: Details
days.work: Add texture and details (eyes, fur, scales) and paint.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Hold a family 'art critique': say one thing you like and one question about each other's sculptures.

days.title: Unit 5 check
days.work: Explain texture, form, and repurposing in your sculpture.

weeks.assessment: Original sculpture and critique participation.

materials: orchestra videos (PBS or BBC Ten Pieces)

days.title: Four families
days.work: Watch an orchestra instrument demonstration and sort picture cards into strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion.

days.title: How sound is made
days.work: Make a rubber-band guitar (string), a straw oboe (woodwind), and a tube trumpet (brass buzz) and compare how each makes sound.

days.title: Timbre game
days.work: Listen to 10 instrument sound clips and name the family of each.

days.title: Favorite instrument
days.work: Research one instrument and draw it, labeling its parts and family.

days.title: Check
days.work: Identify instrument families from sound and picture (10 items).

weeks.assessment: Instrument family identification check.

objectives: Describe how music tells a story
materials: recording of Prokofiev's 'Peter and the Wolf'

days.title: Meet the characters
days.work: Listen to the theme for each character in 'Peter and the Wolf' (bird = flute, duck = oboe, cat = clarinet, wolf = French horns, Peter = strings).

days.title: Listen to the story
days.work: Listen to the full piece and hold up a character card whenever that theme plays.

days.title: Why that instrument
days.work: Explain why Prokofiev chose each instrument for its character (high, quick flute for the bird).

days.title: Draw a scene
days.work: Draw your favorite scene and label the instrument playing.

days.title: Check
days.work: Match 7 themes to characters and instruments.

weeks.assessment: Theme-matching check and labeled drawing.

weeks.topic: Dynamics and tempo: Carnival of the Animals
objectives: Explain how composers use dynamics and tempo

days.title: Dynamics
days.work: Learn forte (loud) and piano (soft) and sing 'Bingo' changing dynamics on signal.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Learn fast (allegro) and slow (largo) and move like animals to 'The Elephant' and 'Wild Horses' from Carnival of the Animals.

days.title: Listening map
days.work: Listen to 'The Swan' and 'Aquarium' and describe dynamics and tempo for each.

days.title: Your animal
days.work: Choose an animal and play it on a homemade instrument with dynamics and tempo that fit; family guesses the animal.

days.title: Check
days.work: Identify dynamics and tempo in 4 excerpts and say which piece you prefer and why.

weeks.assessment: Dynamics and tempo listening check with preference.

weeks.topic: Music in daily life and unit reflection
objectives: Identify uses of music in daily life
materials: recordings of a lullaby, a march, a jingle

days.title: Music everywhere
days.work: List all the music you hear in one day (ads, video games, stores, church, car radio) and its purpose.

days.title: Purpose sort
days.work: Listen to a lullaby, a march, a dance tune, and a jingle and explain how each piece's tempo and dynamics fit its purpose.

days.title: Family playlist
days.work: Interview family about their favorite songs and why they like them; make a family playlist.

days.title: Music and art
days.work: Paint while listening to two contrasting pieces and compare the paintings.

days.title: Unit 6 check
days.work: Tell your favorite piece from the unit, using music words to explain why.

weeks.assessment: Purpose sort and explanation of preferences.

objectives: Learn the cultural use of papel picado

days.title: Papel picado
days.work: Look at photos of papel picado banners used in Mexican celebrations like Día de los Muertos and weddings and discuss their purpose.

days.title: Practice folds
days.work: Practice folding and cutting small shapes from scrap paper to make symmetrical designs.

days.title: Make banners
days.work: Fold and cut 4 tissue-paper flags with designs.

days.title: Hang
days.work: String the flags into a banner and hang it.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare papel picado to decorations your family uses for celebrations.

weeks.assessment: Papel picado banner and comparison.

objectives: Learn the history and purpose of gyotaku
Compare a tradition's past and present uses
materials: rubber fish replica (or a whole fish from the market)

days.title: Gyotaku history
days.work: Learn that Japanese fishermen in the 1800s made gyotaku ('fish rubbing') prints to record the size of their catches, and look at museum examples.

days.title: First prints
days.work: Brush a thin layer of paint on a rubber fish, lay paper over it, and rub gently from head to tail; make 2 prints and compare which shows more scale texture.

days.title: Color experiments
days.work: Make 3 more prints using different paint colors and paper, noting which combination shows the most detail.

days.title: Finish the best print
days.work: Choose the best print, paint in the eye with a fine brush, and add a name stamp or signature as Japanese printmakers do.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Explain in 3 sentences how gyotaku started as a record and became art, and how it connects to the texture rubbings from Unit 5.

weeks.assessment: Finished gyotaku print and written reflection.

weeks.topic: Patterns in textiles and baskets: kente cloth and Native California baskets
objectives: Identify patterns and meanings in textiles and baskets

days.title: Kente cloth
days.work: Look at images of kente cloth from Ghana and learn that weavers choose colors with meanings (gold for wealth, green for growth); describe the patterns.

days.title: Paper weaving
days.work: Cut slits in a paper 'loom' and weave contrasting paper strips over-under to make a kente-inspired pattern with colors chosen for meaning.

days.title: Native California baskets
days.work: Look at Calisphere photos of Pomo baskets, some woven so tightly they hold water, and describe their patterns and everyday and ceremonial uses.

days.title: Coil a basket
days.work: Make a small coiled 'basket' by wrapping yarn around rope or a pipe cleaner and spiraling it into a dish shape.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a T-chart comparing kente cloth and Pomo baskets (materials, patterns, uses, who makes them) and share one similarity aloud.

weeks.assessment: Paper weaving, coiled basket, and comparison chart.

weeks.topic: Murals and public art in communities
objectives: Explain how public art contributes to communities
Design and paint a mural about home or community
materials: photos of California murals (Chicano Park in San Diego, the Great Wall of Los Angeles)

days.title: California murals
days.work: Look at photos of Chicano Park murals and the Great Wall of Los Angeles and discuss what stories they tell and who they are for.

days.title: Local public art
days.work: Find a mural, statue, or sculpture in your community (in person or online), photograph or sketch it, and write who might enjoy it and why.

days.title: Design
days.work: Sketch a mural design that tells a story about your family or community, including people, places, and a pattern border.

days.title: Paint
days.work: Transfer the design to butcher paper and paint it, using a color palette chosen for mood.

days.title: Unit 7 check
days.work: Present the mural to family and explain how public art can make a community stronger; name one cultural art form from this unit and its use.

weeks.assessment: Mural presentation with explanation of public art.

weeks.topic: Creative movement: levels, shapes, and pathways
objectives: Create movement from images and music

days.title: Movement words
days.work: Practice locomotor movements (walk, skip, gallop, slide) and nonlocomotor movements (twist, bend, stretch, swing) and call them out as a family game.

days.title: Levels and shapes
days.work: Freeze in high, middle, and low shapes (curved, straight, twisted) when the music stops; make 6 different statues.

days.title: Pathways
days.work: Lay masking-tape straight, curved, and zigzag pathways and travel each with a different locomotor movement.

days.title: Images to movement
days.work: Create movement inspired by pictures of a storm, a seed growing, and a melting snowman, using scarves.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a 30-second dance with 3 levels, 2 pathways, and a beginning and ending shape.

weeks.assessment: Short dance sequence meeting the movement checklist.

weeks.topic: Story drama: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
objectives: Use voice and body to show characters
materials: The Three Billy Goats Gruff (any version)

days.title: Character bodies
days.work: Read The Three Billy Goats Gruff and practice how each goat and the troll walk, stand, and speak (tiny trip-trap vs. great big stomp).

days.title: Voices
days.work: Practice reading the dialogue with a different voice for each character, changing volume and speed.

days.title: What if?
days.work: Discuss choices characters could make (What if the troll were lonely? What if the goats shared the grass?) and choose one new plot idea.

days.title: Act it out
days.work: Act out the original story with family using a chair as the bridge, then act out the new version.

days.title: Share
days.work: Share both versions informally and tell which choice changed the story most.

weeks.assessment: Participation in guided drama and new-version performance.

weeks.topic: Moving stories: dance, drama, and music together
objectives: Combine movement, music, and drama to tell a story
materials: recording of 'Peter and the Wolf' or 'Carnival of the Animals'

days.title: Choose the story
days.work: Choose a scene from 'Peter and the Wolf' or 'Carnival of the Animals' and list its characters and events.

days.title: Create movement
days.work: Create a movement for each character that matches its music (slinky clarinet cat, heavy elephant).

days.title: Add sound
days.work: Add homemade percussion sound effects and a narrator line for each part of the scene.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the whole piece twice, fixing one problem each time.

days.title: Unit 8 check
days.work: Perform the moving story for family and explain how dance, drama, and music worked together.

weeks.assessment: Moving-story performance and explanation.

weeks.topic: Art about my life: drawing home and community
objectives: Create artwork about events in home and community life

days.title: Memory list
days.work: List 5 favorite events from this year at home or in the community (a birthday, a festival, a hike, a holiday meal) and sketch two.

days.title: Plan the artwork
days.work: Choose one event and plan an artwork using lines, shapes, colors, and textures from earlier units.

days.title: Create
days.work: Create the artwork with mixed media.

days.title: Second piece
days.work: Create a quick second piece about a place in your community (park, library, market) using a different material.

days.title: Exhibit theme
days.work: Lay out all your artworks from the year and sort them into possible exhibit themes (Nature, Me and My Family, Around the World).

weeks.assessment: Two community-life artworks and exhibit theme sort.

weeks.topic: Compose a song about my community
objectives: Compose a short song with rhythm and melody
Document it with notation or recording

days.title: Lyrics
days.work: Write 4 short lines about your community (places, people, sounds).

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Clap the rhythm of the lyrics and write it in ta and ti-ti notation.

days.title: Melody
days.work: Set the words to a sol-mi-la-do melody using Song Maker or a xylophone.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Perform for a family member, get a 'star and wish,' and revise one line or melody spot.

days.title: Record
days.work: Record the revised song and add a percussion ostinato.

weeks.assessment: Recorded community song with notation.

objectives: Choose and prepare artwork for an exhibit
Compare ways to mount and display art
materials: construction paper or cardstock for mats

days.title: Curate
days.work: Choose 6 artworks for the exhibit under one theme and explain why each belongs.

days.title: Mount and mat
days.work: Compare framing options (mats, mounting on cardstock, hanging with clips) and mount each piece.

days.title: Labels
days.work: Make museum-style labels with title, materials, and date.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a 3-sentence artist statement about yourself and your favorite piece.

days.title: Plan the space
days.work: Plan where each piece will hang in your home gallery and sketch a layout.

weeks.assessment: Mounted artworks with labels and artist statement.

days.title: Program
days.work: Choose 3 musical pieces for the showcase (a folk song, your rhythm composition, your community song) and write a program.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse each piece and mark one tricky spot to fix.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Perform for a family member and apply one piece of feedback.

days.title: Invitations
days.work: Design invitations with artwork for family and friends.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Run the whole showcase (gallery tour plus music) from start to finish.

weeks.assessment: Dress rehearsal with checklist.

objectives: Reflect on growth using art and music vocabulary

days.title: Set up
days.work: Hang the exhibit and set up the performance space.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Give a gallery tour and perform the 3 music pieces for guests.

days.title: Audience
days.work: Practice good audience etiquette by watching a family member's performance or talent.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare a fall artwork with a spring artwork and describe your growth using art words.

days.title: Celebrate
days.work: Write a thank-you note to guests and choose one art and one music goal for summer.

weeks.assessment: Showcase performance, gallery tour, and written reflection.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: PE 2
courses.description: PE 2 refines fundamental movement skills: traveling over, under and through obstacles, changing speed and direction, skipping, leaping and jumping, balancing, transferring weight and forward rolls, overhand throwing, catching high and low, hand and foot dribbling, kicking, striking with paddles, jump rope and dance. Children measure their heart rate, track fitness scores in a log, and practice cooperation, fair play and problem solving, ending with a skill showcase and family field day.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards; 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-2.1.1: Travel over, under, in front of, behind, and through objects and obstacles.
standards.PE-2.1.2: Change speed and direction in response to various rhythms and signals.
standards.PE-2.1.3: Balance on a variety of body parts and transfer weight from one body part to another.
standards.PE-2.1.4: Perform a forward roll and combine rolls and balances into a short sequence.
standards.PE-2.1.5: Skip, leap, and jump for distance and height using a mature motor pattern.
standards.PE-2.1.6: Jump a self-turned rope forward and backward, and jump a long rope with a partner.
standards.PE-2.1.7: Throw a ball overhand to a target and to a partner, stepping with the opposite foot.
standards.PE-2.1.8: Catch a thrown ball above the waist and below the waist, including while moving.
standards.PE-2.1.9: Kick a rolling ball and dribble a ball with the feet while walking and jogging.
standards.PE-2.1.10: Strike a ball or balloon with a paddle or the hand, sending it upward and forward with control.
standards.PE-2.1.11: Dribble a ball with one hand while walking, changing hands and direction.
standards.PE-2.1.12: Create and perform rhythmic movement sequences and simple dances, including hoop and ribbon patterns.
standards.PE-2.2.1: Explain how practice improves the performance of a motor skill.
standards.PE-2.2.2: Describe the critical elements (cues) of the skip, leap, and horizontal and vertical jump.
standards.PE-2.2.3: Describe the critical elements of the overhand throw, catching, kicking, and striking.
standards.PE-2.2.4: Identify and use pathways, levels, and force (strong/light) when moving and manipulating objects.
standards.PE-2.3.1: Participate in enjoyable and challenging physical activities in and outside of school.
standards.PE-2.3.2: Participate in moderate to vigorous physical activity for increasing periods of time.
standards.PE-2.3.3: Perform muscular strength and endurance activities (modified push-ups, curl-ups, climbing, hanging).
standards.PE-2.3.4: Perform flexibility exercises that stretch the major muscle groups.
standards.PE-2.3.5: Walk and jog continuously for increasing distances to build aerobic capacity.
standards.PE-2.3.6: Measure heart rate by placing a hand on the chest or neck before and after activity.
standards.PE-2.4.1: Explain that the heart is a muscle that grows stronger with physical activity.
standards.PE-2.4.2: Describe how heart rate and breathing change during and after physical activity.
standards.PE-2.4.3: Identify healthy foods and the need for water before, during, and after physical activity.
standards.PE-2.4.4: Explain that muscles pull on bones to move the body and that stretching keeps muscles flexible.
standards.PE-2.4.5: Identify safety practices for physical activity, including sun protection and proper equipment use.
standards.PE-2.5.1: Work cooperatively with a partner or small group to complete a task or game.
standards.PE-2.5.2: Follow rules, take turns, and accept the results of a game with good sportsmanship.
standards.PE-2.5.3: Give and accept positive feedback and encouragement.
standards.PE-2.5.4: Use simple problem-solving steps to resolve conflicts that arise during play.
standards.PE-2.5.5: Identify positive feelings and challenges that come from participating in physical activity.

units.title: Moving in Space: Direction, Speed and Obstacles
units.big_idea: Changing direction, speed and level helps us move safely and cleverly.

units.title: Skip, Leap and Jump
units.big_idea: Each locomotor skill has cues that make it smoother, farther and higher.

units.title: Balance, Weight Transfer and Rolling
units.big_idea: A tight core and wide base let us balance, transfer weight and roll safely.

units.title: Fitness and My Heart
units.big_idea: My heart is a muscle, and exercise makes it, my lungs and my muscles stronger.

units.title: Overhand Throwing and Catching on the Move
units.big_idea: Side to target, step and follow through to throw; reach, give and watch to catch.

units.title: Dribbling and Kicking
units.big_idea: Soft touches keep the ball close; controlled force sends it where we aim.

units.title: Striking and Volleying
units.big_idea: A flat paddle, watching eyes and the right amount of force control a struck ball.

units.title: Jump Rope, Hoops and Dance
units.big_idea: Moving to a beat builds rhythm, coordination and endurance.

units.title: Cooperative Games and Fair Play
units.big_idea: Teams succeed when everyone follows rules, encourages others and solves problems fairly.

units.title: Fitness Check and Field Day
units.big_idea: We measure our growth and celebrate how active and skillful we have become.

days.title: Warm-up routine
days.work: Learn a 5-move warm-up (jog in place, arm circles, jumping jacks, toe touches, high knees) to use all year; set up a cone boundary in the yard.

days.title: Signal game
days.work: Walk, jog and skip in general space and freeze on the whistle; add 'down' (sit) and 'switch' (change direction) signals.

days.title: Safety & sun
days.work: Make a PE safety checklist: water bottle, sunscreen/hat, clear space, shoes tied; then play Simon Says with movement commands.

days.title: Shadow tag
days.work: Play shadow tag inside the cone boundary, practicing safe tagging (two-finger touch on shoulder).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Respond to 5 random signals without bumping cones and explain two safety rules and why warm-ups come first.

weeks.assessment: Observation: safe spacing and correct response to signals; oral safety rules.

objectives: Move fast, medium and slow on cue
Change direction forward, backward and sideways

days.title: Speed dial
days.work: Move to a drumbeat: slow beats = slow walk, medium = jog, fast = quick feet; switch speeds with the beat.

days.title: Direction drill
days.work: Travel forward, backward and sideways between cones, looking over the shoulder when moving backward.

days.title: Zigzag & curve
days.work: Draw straight, curved and zigzag pathways in chalk and travel each with three different locomotor skills.

days.title: Traffic jam
days.work: Play 'cars and traffic lights': green = fast, yellow = slow, red = stop, 'reverse' = backward, 'turn' = change direction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Follow a 6-part cue card (e.g., slow-zigzag-backward) and draw your favorite pathway.

weeks.assessment: Cue-card sequence performed accurately; pathway drawing.

objectives: Travel over, under, around and through obstacles

days.title: Obstacle words
days.work: Practice going over a pool noodle, under a broom across two chairs, around a cone and through a hoop; name each word.

days.title: Levels
days.work: Travel the course at high (tiptoes), medium and low (crawl) levels; freeze in a shape at each level.

days.title: Build a course
days.work: Design and draw a 6-station obstacle course with a parent and set it up in the yard or living room.

days.title: Timed course
days.work: Run your course three times, timing each try and recording the times on a chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Teach the course to a family member using the words over, under, around, through and explain which level each part used.

weeks.assessment: Course completed safely; correct use of position and level words.

objectives: Combine direction, speed and obstacle skills

days.title: Add a twist
days.work: Add direction changes to your course: sideways shuffle between cones and backward walk on a chalk line.

days.title: Follow the leader
days.work: Play follow the leader with a sibling or parent, taking turns leading with speed and level changes.

days.title: Animal moves
days.work: Move through the course as animals (bear crawl, crab walk, frog jump, flamingo balance).

days.title: Encouragement
days.work: Cheer a family member through your course using 3 positive phrases, then switch roles.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Run the full course and compare with your week-3 time; tell how practice changed your time.

weeks.assessment: Course time comparison and observation of encouraging words.

objectives: Skip with a step-hop and arm swing

days.title: Step-hop
days.work: Break the skip into 'step-hop' slowly on one side, then the other, saying the cue out loud.

days.title: Add arms
days.work: Skip across the yard swinging opposite arm to leg; practice in front of a window or mirror.

days.title: Skip to music
days.work: Skip to a steady song, changing direction each time the chorus starts.

days.title: Skip for height & distance
days.work: Skip high (big lift) and then skip far (long steps); count how many skips it takes to cross the yard.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Show a smooth skip for 20 meters and tell the 3 cues: step-hop, swing arms, land on toes.

weeks.assessment: Skip checklist: step-hop pattern, opposition, rhythm.

objectives: Leap over a low obstacle with a run, take-off and soft landing

days.title: Run and reach
days.work: Run 3 steps and leap over a rolled towel, reaching forward with the lead leg.

days.title: River leap
days.work: Draw a chalk 'river' that gets wider; leap across from the narrow end to the wide end.

days.title: Lead leg switch
days.work: Practice leaping off the right foot and the left foot; note which is stronger.

days.title: Leap series
days.work: Run-run-leap pattern down the yard to a drumbeat; land softly with bent knees.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Leap the widest river you can 3 times, record your best, and explain how a leap differs from a jump.

weeks.assessment: Leap cue checklist and recorded distance.

objectives: Jump with a two-foot take-off and landing
Use arms to jump farther and higher

days.title: Swing and spring
days.work: Practice 'swing arms back, bend knees, swing forward, jump' for standing long jumps; mark each landing with chalk.

days.title: Measure it
days.work: Do 5 standing long jumps, measure the best one in inches, and record it.

days.title: Reach high
days.work: Stand by a wall and jump to tap a sticky note; move the note up when you reach it 3 times.

days.title: Jump patterns
days.work: Jump a chalk hopscotch and a 'jump ladder' (two feet, one foot, side to side).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Retest the long jump and wall jump, compare with Day 2 and explain how practice helped.

weeks.assessment: Recorded jump scores and oral explanation of cues and practice.

objectives: Combine skip, leap, jump and gallop

days.title: Locomotor dice
days.work: Roll a die; each number is a skill (1 hop, 2 gallop, 3 slide, 4 skip, 5 leap, 6 jump) to travel to the next cone.

days.title: Pattern card
days.work: Write a 4-skill pattern (skip-skip-leap-jump) and perform it 5 times without stopping.

days.title: Relay
days.work: Run a family relay where each leg uses a different locomotor skill; pass a beanbag baton.

days.title: Coach me
days.work: Watch a partner skip and leap and tell them one thing they did well and one cue to try.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Demonstrate all six locomotor skills in a row and name one cue for each.

weeks.assessment: Locomotor skill checklist (6 skills) and peer-feedback observation.

objectives: Use a tight core for stability

days.title: Body part balances
days.work: Balance on 5, 4, 3, 2, then 1 body part, holding each for 5 seconds.

days.title: Wide vs. narrow base
days.work: Compare balancing with feet wide and feet together; explain which is easier and why.

days.title: Balance cards
days.work: Draw 6 balance cards (stork, airplane, bridge, tripod, V-sit, frog) and perform them in a shuffled order.

days.title: Partner balance
days.work: Do partner balances (back-to-back sit-stand, hand-to-hand lean) safely with a family member.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Hold 4 different balances for 5 seconds each and explain what a 'tight core' does.

weeks.assessment: Balance hold checklist.

objectives: Walk a narrow surface forward, backward and sideways
Transfer weight from feet to hands

days.title: Beam walk
days.work: Walk a 2x4 board or chalk line forward and sideways with arms out; then try with a beanbag on your head.

days.title: Backward and turns
days.work: Walk the beam backward and practice a half-turn in the middle.

days.title: Feet to hands
days.work: Practice bunny hops (feet to hands to feet) over a rope and a cartwheel-shape step-over on the grass.

days.title: Muscles at work
days.work: Feel your leg and stomach muscles tighten while balancing; learn that muscles pull on bones to move us.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Cross the beam three ways without falling off and show one weight-transfer move.

weeks.assessment: Beam and weight-transfer checklist.

objectives: Perform log, egg and forward rolls safely

days.title: Rolling review
days.work: Practice log rolls and egg rolls on a mat, keeping arms in and body tight.

days.title: Rocking chair
days.work: Rock back and forth in a tuck, chin on chest, to learn the rounded back for a forward roll.

days.title: Forward roll on a slope
days.work: Roll forward down a gentle grass slope or folded mattress: hands down, chin tucked, push with feet.

days.title: Forward roll on flat
days.work: Practice forward rolls on the flat mat with a parent spotting at the hips.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform 2 forward rolls with chin tucked and say the 3 safety cues.

weeks.assessment: Forward-roll checklist: hands placed, chin tucked, rounded back.

objectives: Link balances and rolls into a sequence

days.title: Plan it
days.work: Draw a routine of start shape, balance, roll, balance, finish shape.

days.title: Smooth transitions
days.work: Practice moving from one part of the routine to the next without stopping.

days.title: Add music
days.work: Perform the routine to a short piece of calm music, holding each balance for 3 counts.

days.title: Polish
days.work: Video or have a parent watch; pick one part to improve and practice it 5 times.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the 5-part routine for the family and explain which part was hardest.

weeks.assessment: Routine performance rubric (shapes held, safe roll, smooth transitions).

objectives: Describe how heart rate changes with exercise

days.title: Find your heart
days.work: Place a hand on your chest, feel your heartbeat resting, and learn that the heart is a muscle pumping blood.

days.title: Before and after
days.work: Count heartbeats for 15 seconds at rest, then after 1 minute of jumping jacks; record both.

days.title: Breathing check
days.work: Notice and describe breathing at rest, after walking and after running in place.

days.title: Heart-healthy moves
days.work: Sort activities (sleeping, walking, soccer, dancing, video games) into 'slow heart' and 'fast heart' groups.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain with your chart how exercise changes your heart rate and breathing.

weeks.assessment: Heart-rate chart and oral explanation.

days.title: Walk-jog intervals
days.work: Alternate 1 minute jogging and 1 minute walking for 8 minutes; sip water after.

days.title: Pacing game
days.work: Jog laps at 'turtle' and 'cheetah' pace and decide which pace lasts longer.

days.title: Neighborhood loop
days.work: Walk-jog a neighborhood loop with a parent and record minutes moving without stopping.

days.title: Fuel & water
days.work: Choose a healthy pre-activity snack and drink water before, during and after a 10-minute jog.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Jog or walk-jog continuously for 10 minutes and record the time on your fitness log.

weeks.assessment: Fitness log of continuous minutes.

objectives: Perform modified push-ups, curl-ups and hangs

days.title: Push-up practice
days.work: Practice knee push-ups and wall push-ups with a straight back; count good-form reps.

days.title: Curl-ups
days.work: Do curl-ups sliding fingertips along the mat; count reps in 1 minute.

days.title: Playground strength
days.work: At a park, try hanging from bars, climbing a ladder and doing monkey-bar swings.

days.title: Animal strength circuit
days.work: Do 30 seconds each of bear crawl, crab walk, plank and frog jumps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record push-ups, curl-ups and hang time in your fitness log and name the muscles each works.

weeks.assessment: Baseline strength scores in fitness log.

days.title: Stretch routine
days.work: Learn 6 stretches (hamstring, quad, calf, shoulder, side, butterfly), holding each for 15 seconds.

days.title: Sit and reach
days.work: Measure sit-and-reach with a ruler by a box and record the result.

days.title: Yoga for kids
days.work: Follow a kid yoga video (tree, cat-cow, downward dog, cobra) and name which muscles stretch.

days.title: Fitness circuit
days.work: Do a 6-station circuit: jog, push-ups, curl-ups, jumping jacks, stretch, balance.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how cardio, strength and flexibility each help your body; share your fitness log.

weeks.assessment: Fitness log complete; oral explanation of 3 fitness parts.

objectives: Throw overhand with side to target and opposite step

days.title: T-pose throw
days.work: Learn cues: side to target, arm back in a 'T', step with opposite foot, throw and follow through.

days.title: Wall throws
days.work: Throw tennis balls overhand at a taped square on a wall from 10 feet, 10 times.

days.title: Distance throws
days.work: Throw for distance in the yard and mark the best of 5 throws.

days.title: Target game
days.work: Knock down a pyramid of plastic cups with overhand throws; count throws needed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Throw overhand 5 times while a parent checks off the 4 cues.

weeks.assessment: Overhand throw cue checklist.

objectives: Catch above the waist (thumbs together) and below (pinkies together)

days.title: Scarf catching
days.work: Toss and catch scarves high and low to practice tracking with your eyes.

days.title: Thumbs and pinkies
days.work: Catch tossed balls above the waist with thumbs together and below with pinkies together.

days.title: Soft hands
days.work: Practice 'giving' with your arms to pull the ball in; play egg-toss with a water balloon or bean bag.

days.title: Self-toss
days.work: Toss and catch to yourself, adding a clap, then a spin, before the catch.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Catch 8 of 10 tosses at mixed heights and explain thumbs vs. pinkies.

weeks.assessment: Catch count out of 10 and cue explanation.

days.title: Target hands
days.work: Throw overhand to a partner's 'target hands'; step back one big step after 3 good catches.

days.title: Moving catch
days.work: Shuffle sideways to catch a ball tossed to the side.

days.title: Count-up challenge
days.work: With a partner, count consecutive throw-catch pairs and try to beat your record.

days.title: Monkey in the middle
days.work: Play a 3-person throw-and-catch game, practicing quick throws to an open partner.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete 10 throws and catches with a partner at 15 feet and set a record goal.

weeks.assessment: Partner record and observation of throw/catch cues.

objectives: Apply throwing and catching in games

days.title: Basket toss
days.work: Throw beanbags into laundry baskets at 3 distances for points.

days.title: Clean your room
days.work: Play a family game throwing soft balls over a 'net' (couch cushions) before the timer ends.

days.title: Hot potato
days.work: Play hot potato with quick catch-and-throw passes.

days.title: Practice graph
days.work: Retake the wall-target test from week 17 and graph both scores.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain with your graph how practice changed your throwing accuracy.

weeks.assessment: Before/after accuracy graph.

objectives: Dribble with fingertips at waist height

days.title: Fingertip pads
days.work: Dribble in place with the dominant hand using fingertips, ball at waist height, 20 times.

days.title: Switch hands
days.work: Dribble with the weaker hand, then alternate hands every 5 bounces.

days.title: Walking dribble
days.work: Dribble while walking a straight line, then a curved chalk path.

days.title: Eyes up
days.work: Dribble while calling out the number of fingers a parent holds up.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Dribble while walking around 4 cones and back, switching hands once.

weeks.assessment: Dribble checklist: fingertips, waist height, eyes up.

objectives: Dribble a ball with soft touches using inside and outside of foot

days.title: Toe taps
days.work: Do toe taps on top of the ball and inside-foot passes between feet.

days.title: Walking dribble
days.work: Dribble the ball with soft touches while walking, keeping it close.

days.title: Cone weave
days.work: Dribble through a zigzag of 6 cones using inside and outside of foot.

days.title: Red light/green light
days.work: Dribble on green and stop the ball with the sole of your foot on red.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Dribble through the cone course without losing control and explain strong vs. light touches.

weeks.assessment: Cone-weave dribble observation.

objectives: Kick a rolling ball with inside of foot

days.title: Plant and kick
days.work: Learn cues: plant foot beside ball, kick with inside of foot, follow through to target.

days.title: Rolling ball kick
days.work: Kick a ball rolled slowly toward you back to the roller.

days.title: Force control
days.work: Kick to cones at 5, 10 and 20 feet, using light, medium and strong kicks.

days.title: Mini goal
days.work: Shoot at a 2-cone goal from 3 spots; count goals out of 9.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Pass back and forth with a partner 10 times and name the 3 kick cues.

weeks.assessment: Kick cue checklist and goal count.

objectives: Use dribbling and passing in small games

days.title: Pass and move
days.work: Pass to a partner, then move to a new open spot to receive the next pass.

days.title: Dribble tag
days.work: Play dribble tag where everyone dribbles (by hand) and tries to tag others' balls out.

days.title: 2 vs. 1 soccer
days.work: Play a short 2 vs. 1 game with a family member defending.

days.title: Basketball stations
days.work: Rotate: stationary dribble, walking dribble, bounce pass, chest pass.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Show a hand dribble, foot dribble and pass and tell how you helped your teammate.

weeks.assessment: Skill station checklist; self-reflection on teamwork.

objectives: Strike a balloon upward with hands

days.title: Balloon keep-up
days.work: Keep a balloon up with flat hands for as many hits as possible.

days.title: Body parts
days.work: Strike the balloon with hand, elbow, knee and foot in a pattern.

days.title: Partner volley
days.work: Volley a balloon back and forth over a string 'net' with a partner.

days.title: Beach ball
days.work: Move to a beach ball and strike it upward with two hands (set) 10 times.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Keep a balloon up for 15 hits in your space and explain why a flat hand helps.

weeks.assessment: Keep-up count and observation.

objectives: Strike a balloon and ball with a short-handled paddle
materials: short paddles (or paper plate on a paint stick)

days.title: Make a paddle
days.work: Make a paddle from a paper plate and paint stick; practice ready position.

days.title: Up-ups
days.work: Strike a balloon upward with the paddle 10 times, flat face up.

days.title: Down-ups
days.work: Bounce a foam ball down with the paddle, then try alternating up and down.

days.title: Wall rally
days.work: Hit a foam ball to a wall after one bounce and track how many in a row.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Do 10 balloon up-ups and 5 ball bounces and name the paddle cues.

weeks.assessment: Paddle skill counts.

objectives: Strike toward a target with control

days.title: Target strike
days.work: Hit a foam ball off a cone/tee into a hula hoop zone with a paddle or bat.

days.title: Rally count
days.work: Rally a balloon with a partner over a string net, counting together.

days.title: Paddle golf
days.work: Hit a ball along the ground with a paddle through cone 'holes.'

days.title: Coach a partner
days.work: Give a family member 2 positive tips while they practice striking.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play a short rally game, record your best rally and reflect on your striking skill.

weeks.assessment: Best rally score and feedback observation.

objectives: Jump a self-turned rope forward and backward

days.title: Rope sizing & turns
days.work: Size the rope (handles to armpits), then practice turn-stop-jump over the rope.

days.title: Continuous forward
days.work: Jump forward continuously, counting jumps in 30 seconds.

days.title: Backward jumps
days.work: Practice turning the rope backward and jumping over it.

days.title: Long rope
days.work: Jump a long rope turned by two family members; try running in.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record most forward jumps in a row and try 5 backward jumps.

weeks.assessment: Jump-count log.

objectives: Create rhythmic patterns with hoops and ribbons

days.title: Hoop skills
days.work: Practice waist hooping, arm hooping and rolling a hoop and chasing it.

days.title: Ribbon shapes
days.work: Make circles, figure eights, snakes and spirals with a ribbon stick to music.

days.title: Pattern build
days.work: Create an 8-count pattern with the hoop or ribbon and repeat it 4 times.

days.title: Jump rope chant
days.work: Learn a jump rope rhyme (e.g., 'Teddy Bear, Teddy Bear') and jump to it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform your hoop or ribbon pattern and tell how it made you feel.

weeks.assessment: Pattern performance and reflection.

objectives: Learn a simple folk or line dance

days.title: Folk dance
days.work: Learn a simple folk dance like the Chimes of Dunkirk or a children's line dance from a video.

days.title: Freeze dance
days.work: Play freeze dance, holding a balanced shape when the music stops.

days.title: Create a dance
days.work: Create a 16-count dance using skips, slides, turns and a jump.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice your dance to music 3 times and add a beginning and ending pose.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform your dance for family and explain which moves raised your heart rate.

weeks.assessment: Dance performance rubric.

objectives: Work with others to solve movement challenges

days.title: Hoop pass
days.work: Pass a hula hoop around a hand-holding circle without letting go.

days.title: Blanket ball
days.work: Use a blanket with a partner to toss and catch a ball together.

days.title: Lava crossing
days.work: Cross the yard on 'stepping stones' (paper plates) as a team without touching the 'lava.'

days.title: Team juggle
days.work: Toss a ball in the same order around the family, adding a second ball.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one way your team cooperated and one thing you would do differently.

weeks.assessment: Cooperation reflection.

days.title: Rules matter
days.work: Play tag with no rules, then with rules; discuss why rules make games fair and safe.

days.title: Win or lose
days.work: Play capture the flag; practice saying 'good game' whether you win or lose.

days.title: Solve it
days.work: Learn problem-solving steps (stop, talk, choose a fair fix like rock-paper-scissors or a redo) and role-play an 'out or not out' dispute.

days.title: Make a game
days.work: Invent a game with 3 rules and teach it to the family.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play your invented game and show good sportsmanship and fair problem solving.

weeks.assessment: Observation of sportsmanship and problem-solving steps.

objectives: Play traditional games with skill and fair play
Choose activities to do outside of school

days.title: Hopscotch
days.work: Play hopscotch with correct hopping and jumping and fair turns.

days.title: Four square
days.work: Learn and play four square or a two-square version with a partner.

days.title: Kickball
days.work: Play a mini kickball game using kicking, throwing and catching.

days.title: Activity plan
days.work: Make a list of 5 games you can play at home or the park and schedule two.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play one game from your list and tell why it is fun and good exercise.

weeks.assessment: Activity plan and game play.

objectives: Retest strength, flexibility and endurance and compare

days.title: Strength retest
days.work: Retest push-ups, curl-ups and hang time and record them next to week-15 scores.

days.title: Flexibility retest
days.work: Retest sit-and-reach and record.

days.title: Endurance retest
days.work: Walk-jog continuously as long as possible up to 15 minutes; record minutes and heart rate.

days.title: Graph progress
days.work: Make a bar graph comparing fall and spring fitness scores.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Set one summer fitness goal based on your graph.

weeks.assessment: Fitness retest and goal.

objectives: Show mastery of locomotor and manipulative skills

days.title: Locomotor test
days.work: Perform skip, leap, gallop, slide and standing long jump; parent uses checklist.

days.title: Throw & catch
days.work: Show overhand throw to a target and catches high and low.

days.title: Dribble & kick
days.work: Show hand dribble around cones and kick to a target.

days.title: Strike & rope
days.work: Show paddle up-ups and jump rope forward.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-rate each skill with a smiley scale and pick one to keep practicing.

weeks.assessment: End-of-year skill checklist and self-rating.

objectives: Plan and lead a field day

days.title: Plan stations
days.work: Plan 6 field-day stations (sack race, beanbag toss, relay, long jump, three-legged race, water balloon toss).

days.title: Make awards
days.work: Make ribbons for effort, teamwork and sportsmanship.

days.title: Field day
days.work: Lead family or friends through all stations, with water breaks and sunscreen.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write or draw your favorite part of PE this year and how you got stronger.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present your PE portfolio (fitness log, graphs, reflections) to family.

weeks.assessment: Field-day leadership and PE portfolio.

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health 2
courses.description: Health 2 helps children build healthy habits and safe choices: naming and managing feelings, friendship, standing up to bullying and appreciating families; germs, dental care, sleep and sun protection; MyPlate, breakfast, snacks, food labels, farm-to-table and food safety; daily activity and screen balance; body systems and growth; pedestrian, bike, water, fire, earthquake and personal safety; medicine, poison, tobacco and alcohol awareness; and community health helpers and a healthy environment.
courses.framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards; 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-2.1.1.M: Identify a variety of feelings and describe healthy ways to express and cope with them.
standards.H-2.1.2.M: Describe qualities of a good friend and ways to include others.
standards.H-2.1.3.M: Explain how families and family members are different and how they support one another.
standards.H-2.4.1.M: Demonstrate listening skills and 'I-messages' to resolve conflicts and express feelings.
standards.H-2.4.2.M: Demonstrate how to respond to bullying, including telling a trusted adult and helping others.
standards.H-2.7.1.M: Practice strategies to manage stress and strong emotions (deep breathing, counting, asking for help).
standards.H-2.1.1.P: Explain how germs cause illness and how handwashing, covering coughs, and vaccines help prevent disease.
standards.H-2.1.2.P: Describe proper dental care, including brushing, flossing, limiting sugary foods, and the role of dentists.
standards.H-2.1.3.P: Explain why adequate sleep, rest, and limited screen time are important for health.
standards.H-2.1.4.P: Describe ways to protect skin, eyes, and ears (sun protection, eye safety, loud noise).
standards.H-2.3.1.P: Identify trusted adults and health professionals in the community who promote health.
standards.H-2.6.1.P: Set a personal health goal (e.g., brushing twice daily) and track progress.
standards.H-2.7.1.P: Demonstrate personal hygiene and dental-care practices.
standards.H-2.8.1.P: Encourage others to reduce, reuse, and recycle and to keep the environment healthy.
standards.H-2.1.1.N: Identify the five food groups on MyPlate and recommended daily amounts for children.
standards.H-2.1.2.N: Describe the benefits of eating a variety of fruits and vegetables and drinking water.
standards.H-2.1.3.N: Explain the importance of eating breakfast and choosing healthy snacks low in added sugar, fat, and salt.
standards.H-2.1.4.N: Identify where food comes from and how it gets from farms to the table.
standards.H-2.1.5.N: Explain how physical activity and limiting screen time benefit the body and mind.
standards.H-2.2.1.N: Explain how media and advertising influence food choices.
standards.H-2.3.1.N: Use simple information on food labels (serving size, sugar) to compare foods.
standards.H-2.5.1.N: Use a decision-making process to choose healthy meals and snacks.
standards.H-2.6.1.N: Set a goal to increase daily physical activity or healthy food choices and monitor progress.
standards.H-2.7.1.N: Practice food safety: handwashing, washing produce, and keeping foods at safe temperatures.
standards.H-2.1.1.G: Describe the basic structure and functions of the skeletal, muscular, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems.
standards.H-2.1.2.G: Explain that people grow and develop at different rates and that each person is unique.
standards.H-2.1.3.G: Describe how the senses work and how to protect sense organs.
standards.H-2.1.4.G: Identify life stages (infant, child, teen, adult, older adult) and how needs change.
standards.H-2.1.1.S: Identify safety rules for walking, biking, riding in vehicles, and using playgrounds.
standards.H-2.1.2.S: Describe fire, earthquake, and emergency safety, including a family emergency plan and kit.
standards.H-2.1.3.S: Explain water and sun safety rules.
standards.H-2.1.4.S: Distinguish between safe and unsafe touch and situations, including online and with strangers.
standards.H-2.1.5.S: Identify dangers of weapons and what to do if a weapon is found.
standards.H-2.4.1.S: Demonstrate how to call 911, give accurate information, and ask a trusted adult for help.
standards.H-2.7.1.S: Practice safety behaviors such as wearing a helmet, using a seat belt or booster seat, and following drills.
standards.H-2.1.1.A: Explain the difference between medicines and other drugs and the rules for using medicines safely.
standards.H-2.1.2.A: Identify household products that are poisonous and how to read warning labels.
standards.H-2.1.3.A: Describe the harmful effects of tobacco, vaping, secondhand smoke, and alcohol on the body.
standards.H-2.2.1.A: Identify how family, friends, and media influence decisions about alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs.
standards.H-2.4.1.A: Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid unsafe substances and situations.
